evidence.paraphrase: Mudgala resumes Brahmā’s creation: Brahmins from mouth, Kṣatriyas arms, Vaiśyas thighs, Śūdras feet; renunciation from head, forest-stage heart, brahmacarya navel and household-state lower legs. Dharma chest and Adharma back set god/demon courses; gods/Gandharvas/Apsarases/Yakṣas/Asuras/Yātudhānas, snakes/birds/beasts/humans arise from his body. They act yet do not multiply. These are source-local cosmological body-emergences, not universal biological descent claims.
evidence.verifier: Mudgala continuation4 author, direct Sanskrit body
evidence.verification_notes: Read actual cited body; attributed dialogue kept distinct from narrator fact. Independent root review pending.

evidence.paraphrase: Mudgala classifies nine creations: first mahat, second tanmātra/bhūta, third vaikārika/indriya (three prākṛta); fourth stationary beings, fifth tiryak, sixth upward-flow gods, seventh downward-flow humans, eighth bhautika beings, ninth kaumāra (six vaikṛta). The first three are described as buddhi-pūrva, guiding creatures through principles. Brahmā is distressed that his diverse creatures do not multiply.
evidence.verifier: Mudgala continuation4 author, direct Sanskrit body
evidence.verification_notes: Read actual cited body; attributed dialogue kept distinct from narrator fact. Independent root review pending.

evidence.paraphrase: A couple emerges from Brahmā: Śatarūpā from left limb and Svāyambhuva Manu from right, first knowledgeable in Kṣatriya dharma. They ask orders; he directs sexual procreation through tapas. They bow, go to forest and practice intense Gaṇeśa meditation. Kardama emerges from Brahmā’s shadow, is ordered to create, then goes to forest desiring progeny and meditates on white-form Viṣṇu with prescribed tapas.
evidence.verifier: Mudgala continuation4 author, direct Sanskrit body
evidence.verification_notes: Read actual cited body; attributed dialogue kept distinct from narrator fact. Independent root review pending.

evidence.paraphrase: During this interval Madhu and Kaiṭabha arise from Viṣṇu’s ear dirt, conquer three worlds by arm strength and scatter terrified gods. They approach to eat Brahmā; Brahmā hymns Nidrā and she releases sleeping/unmanifest Viṣṇu, who rises. Viṣṇu wrestles them5000 years without defeating them; the powerful pair crushes him. He conceals himself, flees, takes Śaṅkara’s refuge, bows, narrates the battle and asks a victory method.

evidence.paraphrase: Śiva says Viṣṇu forgot Gaṇeśa and should worship for siddhi. He gives the six-syllable great Gaṇeśa mantra. Viṣṇu goes to Daṇḍakāraṇya, sits in lotus posture, meditates on Gaṇeśa and performs intense tapas by the six-syllable procedure1000 years. Gaṇeśa comes to grant; Viṣṇu joyfully bows, worships and begins hymn. The chapter does not explicitly label these1000 years divine.

evidence.paraphrase: Viṣṇu hymns Gaṇeśa as protector, Siddhi/Buddhi lord, remover of devotee obstacles and obstacle-giver to nondevotees, qualified/unqualified cosmic/acosmic Brahman, human-elephant form, cause/beyond cause, Jyeṣṭharāja, yoga giver in yogin hearts, māyā support and deluder of māyā-makers. He says grace gives intellect/praise, sight makes him Brahman-formed/yoga-giver; he dances with tears/raised hair. Gaṇeśa offers wishes pleased by tapas/devotion and promises hymn reciters/hearers all siddhis, four human aims and immediate desired ends through grace.

evidence.paraphrase: Viṣṇu requests rare unwavering devotion, incomparable knowledge, universal fame and varied strength, destruction-method for Madhu/Kaiṭabha and strength against other demons. Gaṇeśa assents, sends him to battle promising victory by strength. He reveals Brahmā, pleased by the pair’s tapas, kept their death very secret at boon-granting: when they themselves speak death, kill them by that stated mode. He says taking māyā and residing in their and Viṣṇu’s hearts he will bring them under Viṣṇu’s control; when Viṣṇu remembers him he will know the victory-method. The original demons’ request/tapas details and exact death words are not narrated here.

evidence.paraphrase: Gaṇeśa disappears. Viṣṇu establishes a great image with good Brahmins, worships richly; the place becomes Siddhikṣetra, renowned for siddhis through observance and served by siddhas. He resides/worships there devotedly with wife and entourage, then bows and hastens to battle. Meditating on Gaṇeśa he cuts the two powerful demons. No named cutting weapon, thighs/dry-place condition or final death dialogue is supplied in this chapter.

evidence.paraphrase: Nine Brahmā sons perform1000 DIVINE years of heart-Gaṇeśa tapas by one-syllable procedure, daily worship and wind alone as food. Mouse-mounted Gaṇeśa comes, luminous yet gentle. Led by Dakṣa they hymn him as witness/self/yoga/peace, creation-preservation-destruction, all gods, beings/elements/food, cit/bodha/videha/asat/sat/sama/Svānanda/ayoga/yoga and Cintāmaṇi of mental activities. He offers boons and promises faithful hymn users all siddhis, progeny/spouse, infertility removal, wealth/grain/cattle, enjoyment/liberation/Brahman and desired ends. They request unwavering devotion destroying delusion, incomparable creation capacity and success in whatever they wish; he assents, vanishes, and they return to their places meditating on him.

evidence.paraphrase: Brahmā directs Dakṣa to worship Śakti so she becomes his daughter. After100 years Śakti appears; Dakṣa hymns her as māyā/delusion, mother/life-giver, Pārvatī/Gāyatrī/Sāvitrī/Prakṛti/Puruṣa and guṇa support, requesting daughterhood. She grants future daughterhood in many forms and filling the world through offspring, promises her hymn’s readers/hearers all wishes, and vanishes. Mudgala then addresses current Dakṣa: he abandoned Gaṇeśa name/mantra, scorned Satī who became ash, was made sorrowful by Vighneśa, but prior impressions restored memory. Kingship prosperity induces proud blindness/destroys knowledge, so sages avoid it; hear the present account devotedly.

evidence.paraphrase: Manu and Śatarūpā bow to Brahmā and depart at his order; Manu rules dharmically, armed and fond of Gaṇapatyas. Through sexual union they produce sons Priyavrata/Uttānapāda and daughters Ākūti/Devahūti/Prasūti. He gives Prasūti to Dakṣa, Ākūti to Ruci and Devahūti to Kardama. Kardama’s100-year Viṣṇu tapas gains appearance; he asks Viṣṇu as son, receives grant, and Viṣṇu as Kapila becomes his son in Devahūti. Ruci’s mānasa twin Yajña/Dakṣiṇā is born in Ākūti; Yajña Viṣṇu fathers12 Yāma gods in Dakṣiṇā. With wife/sages he makes a jeweled four-armed Gaṇeśa image, constantly worships by yoga; Gaṇeśa gives marvelous yoga. Yajña becomes foremost Gaṇapatya yogin, chants Heramba and teaches disciples Gaṇapatya yoga.

evidence.paraphrase: Dakṣa fathers24 daughters in Prasūti, all Śakti portions/mothers. At Brahmā’s direction he gives13 to Dharma: Śraddhā,Lakṣmī,Dhṛti,Tuṣṭi,Puṣṭi,Medhā,Kriyā,Buddhi,Lajjā,Vapus,Śānti,Siddhi,Kīrti. Their Dharma sons respectively are Kāma,Artha,Niyama,Santoṣa,Lābha,Śama; Kriyā has Daṇḍa/Samaya; Buddhi Bodha/Apramāda; Lajjā Vinaya; Vapus Vyavasāya; Śānti Kṣema; Siddhi Siddha; Kīrti Yaśas. Kāma’s sons are Harṣa/Ānanda. These named daughter-personifications are retained in this Dharma lineage, without silently merging same-named Lakṣmī/Siddhi/Buddhi from other manifestation contexts.

evidence.paraphrase: Brahmā’s back yields couple Adharma/Hiṃsā. Their son Anṛta and daughter Nikṛti yield Bhaya/Naraka and daughters Māyā/Vedanā. Bhaya fathers all-removing Mṛtyu in Māyā; Naraka fathers worldly Duḥkha in Venā (27 raw spelling); equation with adjacent26 Vedanā is a contextual proposal, not verified identity. Mṛtyu yields Vyādhi/Jarā/Śoka/Tṛṣṇā/Krodha. These sorrow-producing Adharma descendants are said to have no further progeny and be ūrdhvaretas. Source-local personified genealogy is not merged with generic delusion/anger concepts.

Śaṅkara fathers Kārttikeya IN SATĪ here, appointed commander by Brahmā. Bhṛgu/Khyāti produce Lakṣmī beloved of Nārāyaṇa and Dhātṛ/Vidhātṛ, Meru’s sons-in-law. This source-local Satī motherhood is retained despite common accounts assigning another maternal form; no universal genealogy imposed.

evidence.paraphrase: Datta, Viṣṇu kalāṃśa, attains successive Brahman/yoga states such as inert/mad/piśāca/child-joy states. People of all varṇas/āśramas serve him, leaving no rest; distressed he submerges by yoga while they wait at shore. By siddhi he manifests Mokṣalakṣmī, rises holding her at left and wine-pot in right, drinks/enjoys with her. They judge him fallen and abandon him, allowing peaceful yoga. evidence.paraphrase: Śaunaka asks why head contact with Mokṣalakṣmī harms demons. Sūta gives Vyāsa-derived explanation: these rajas/tamas demons seek enjoyment, steal/commit sexual misconduct, harm beings, drink and revile sages/gods/scriptures; they reject liberation and honor Bhogalakṣmī with heads. Sages/gods seek liberation, honor her at head. Demons’ yogin contact brings Mokṣalakṣmī, but without desire for liberation and while vicious/pleasure-attached she is angry and destroys them; taking unwanted liberation is treated as striking her with feet. Enjoyment-seekers should honor enjoyment goddess; liberation-seekers similarly reject enjoyment. Bhogalakṣmī is vāsanā-full, Mokṣalakṣmī without vāsanā. These are attributed yogic interpretations, not a universal physical head-contact rule.

narrative_events.details: Mudgala resumes Brahmā’s creation: Brahmins from mouth, Kṣatriyas arms, Vaiśyas thighs, Śūdras feet; renunciation from head, forest-stage heart, brahmacarya navel and household-state lower legs. Dharma chest and Adharma back set god/demon courses; gods/Gandharvas/Apsarases/Yakṣas/Asuras/Yātudhānas, snakes/birds/beasts/humans arise from his body. They act yet do not multiply. These are source-local cosmological body-emergences, not universal biological descent claims.

Mudgala classifies nine creations: first mahat, second tanmātra/bhūta, third vaikārika/indriya (three prākṛta); fourth stationary beings, fifth tiryak, sixth upward-flow gods, seventh downward-flow humans, eighth bhautika beings, ninth kaumāra (six vaikṛta). The first three are described as buddhi-pūrva, guiding creatures through principles. Brahmā is distressed that his diverse creatures do not multiply.

A couple emerges from Brahmā: Śatarūpā from left limb and Svāyambhuva Manu from right, first knowledgeable in Kṣatriya dharma. They ask orders; he directs sexual procreation through tapas. They bow, go to forest and practice intense Gaṇeśa meditation. Kardama emerges from Brahmā’s shadow, is ordered to create, then goes to forest desiring progeny and meditates on white-form Viṣṇu with prescribed tapas.

During this interval Madhu and Kaiṭabha arise from Viṣṇu’s ear dirt, conquer three worlds by arm strength and scatter terrified gods. They approach to eat Brahmā; Brahmā hymns Nidrā and she releases sleeping/unmanifest Viṣṇu, who rises. Viṣṇu wrestles them5000 years without defeating them; the powerful pair crushes him. He conceals himself, flees, takes Śaṅkara’s refuge, bows, narrates the battle and asks a victory method.

Śiva says Viṣṇu forgot Gaṇeśa and should worship for siddhi. He gives the six-syllable great Gaṇeśa mantra. Viṣṇu goes to Daṇḍakāraṇya, sits in lotus posture, meditates on Gaṇeśa and performs intense tapas by the six-syllable procedure1000 years. Gaṇeśa comes to grant; Viṣṇu joyfully bows, worships and begins hymn. The chapter does not explicitly label these1000 years divine.

Viṣṇu hymns Gaṇeśa as protector, Siddhi/Buddhi lord, remover of devotee obstacles and obstacle-giver to nondevotees, qualified/unqualified cosmic/acosmic Brahman, human-elephant form, cause/beyond cause, Jyeṣṭharāja, yoga giver in yogin hearts, māyā support and deluder of māyā-makers. He says grace gives intellect/praise, sight makes him Brahman-formed/yoga-giver; he dances with tears/raised hair. Gaṇeśa offers wishes pleased by tapas/devotion and promises hymn reciters/hearers all siddhis, four human aims and immediate desired ends through grace.

Viṣṇu requests rare unwavering devotion, incomparable knowledge, universal fame and varied strength, destruction-method for Madhu/Kaiṭabha and strength against other demons. Gaṇeśa assents, sends him to battle promising victory by strength. He reveals Brahmā, pleased by the pair’s tapas, kept their death very secret at boon-granting: when they themselves speak death, kill them by that stated mode. He says taking māyā and residing in their and Viṣṇu’s hearts he will bring them under Viṣṇu’s control; when Viṣṇu remembers him he will know the victory-method. The original demons’ request/tapas details and exact death words are not narrated here.

Gaṇeśa disappears. Viṣṇu establishes a great image with good Brahmins, worships richly; the place becomes Siddhikṣetra, renowned for siddhis through observance and served by siddhas. He resides/worships there devotedly with wife and entourage, then bows and hastens to battle. Meditating on Gaṇeśa he cuts the two powerful demons. No named cutting weapon, thighs/dry-place condition or final death dialogue is supplied in this chapter.
narrative_events.outcome: Viṣṇu cuts both demons while meditating on Gaṇeśa; narrator does not give detailed final duel or death speech.

narrative_events.details: Nine Brahmā sons perform1000 DIVINE years of heart-Gaṇeśa tapas by one-syllable procedure, daily worship and wind alone as food. Mouse-mounted Gaṇeśa comes, luminous yet gentle. Led by Dakṣa they hymn him as witness/self/yoga/peace, creation-preservation-destruction, all gods, beings/elements/food, cit/bodha/videha/asat/sat/sama/Svānanda/ayoga/yoga and Cintāmaṇi of mental activities. He offers boons and promises faithful hymn users all siddhis, progeny/spouse, infertility removal, wealth/grain/cattle, enjoyment/liberation/Brahman and desired ends. They request unwavering devotion destroying delusion, incomparable creation capacity and success in whatever they wish; he assents, vanishes, and they return to their places meditating on him.

Brahmā directs Dakṣa to worship Śakti so she becomes his daughter. After100 years Śakti appears; Dakṣa hymns her as māyā/delusion, mother/life-giver, Pārvatī/Gāyatrī/Sāvitrī/Prakṛti/Puruṣa and guṇa support, requesting daughterhood. She grants future daughterhood in many forms and filling the world through offspring, promises her hymn’s readers/hearers all wishes, and vanishes. Mudgala then addresses current Dakṣa: he abandoned Gaṇeśa name/mantra, scorned Satī who became ash, was made sorrowful by Vighneśa, but prior impressions restored memory. Kingship prosperity induces proud blindness/destroys knowledge, so sages avoid it; hear the present account devotedly.

Svāyambhuva Manu with wife goes to forest, performs intense tapas by eight-syllable procedure1000 DIVINE years and gains Gaṇeśa’s appearance. He bows, worships and hymns elephant/Human-elephant/Oṃ form, four arms, mouse vehicle, Svānanda, Siddhi/Buddhi and yoga, saying vision inspires praise and blesses father/tapas/knowledge/lineage/learning/vows. Gaṇeśa raises him, offers a boon and promises his hymn readers/hearers all ends, progeny/prosperity, sorrow removal, wealth/grain, four aims/Brahman and firm devotion.

Manu requests firm Gaṇeśa devotion eliminating delusion, capacity to create, excellent dharma maintenance, lasting protection of subjects, success in every wish and continual dwelling among Gaṇeśa devotees. Gaṇeśa assents to Manu, vanishes and goes to his own realm.

Manu and Śatarūpā bow to Brahmā and depart at his order; Manu rules dharmically, armed and fond of Gaṇapatyas. Through sexual union they produce sons Priyavrata/Uttānapāda and daughters Ākūti/Devahūti/Prasūti. He gives Prasūti to Dakṣa, Ākūti to Ruci and Devahūti to Kardama. Kardama’s100-year Viṣṇu tapas gains appearance; he asks Viṣṇu as son, receives grant, and Viṣṇu as Kapila becomes his son in Devahūti. Ruci’s mānasa twin Yajña/Dakṣiṇā is born in Ākūti; Yajña Viṣṇu fathers12 Yāma gods in Dakṣiṇā. With wife/sages he makes a jeweled four-armed Gaṇeśa image, constantly worships by yoga; Gaṇeśa gives marvelous yoga. Yajña becomes foremost Gaṇapatya yogin, chants Heramba and teaches disciples Gaṇapatya yoga.

Dakṣa fathers24 daughters in Prasūti, all Śakti portions/mothers. At Brahmā’s direction he gives13 to Dharma: Śraddhā,Lakṣmī,Dhṛti,Tuṣṭi,Puṣṭi,Medhā,Kriyā,Buddhi,Lajjā,Vapus,Śānti,Siddhi,Kīrti. Their Dharma sons respectively are Kāma,Artha,Niyama,Santoṣa,Lābha,Śama; Kriyā has Daṇḍa/Samaya; Buddhi Bodha/Apramāda; Lajjā Vinaya; Vapus Vyavasāya; Śānti Kṣema; Siddhi Siddha; Kīrti Yaśas. Kāma’s sons are Harṣa/Ānanda. These named daughter-personifications are retained in this Dharma lineage, without silently merging same-named Lakṣmī/Siddhi/Buddhi from other manifestation contexts.

Brahmā’s back yields couple Adharma/Hiṃsā. Their son Anṛta and daughter Nikṛti yield Bhaya/Naraka and daughters Māyā/Vedanā. Bhaya fathers all-removing Mṛtyu in Māyā; Naraka fathers worldly Duḥkha in Venā (27 raw spelling); equation with adjacent26 Vedanā is a contextual proposal, not verified identity. Mṛtyu yields Vyādhi/Jarā/Śoka/Tṛṣṇā/Krodha. These sorrow-producing Adharma descendants are said to have no further progeny and be ūrdhvaretas. Source-local personified genealogy is not merged with generic delusion/anger concepts.

The remaining11 Dakṣa daughters are married: Satī to Rudra, Khyāti/Bhṛgu, Sambhūti/Marīci, Smṛti/Aṅgiras, Prīti/Pulastya, Kṣamā/Pulaha, Santati/Kratu, Anasūyā/Atri, Ūrjā/Vasiṣṭha, Svāhā/Vahni, Svadhā/Pitṛs. Śaṅkara fathers Kārttikeya IN SATĪ here, appointed commander by Brahmā. Bhṛgu/Khyāti produce Lakṣmī beloved of Nārāyaṇa and Dhātṛ/Vidhātṛ, Meru’s sons-in-law. This source-local Satī motherhood is retained despite common accounts assigning another maternal form; no universal genealogy imposed.

Meru has daughters Ayati/Niyati; in them Dhātṛ/Vidhātṛ have two sons Mṛkaṇḍa/Prāṇa. Mārkaṇḍeya is Mṛkaṇḍa’s son; Vedaśiras is Prāṇa’s. The stanza supplies paired fathers/mothers and paired sons but the individual pair-to-son assignment is not separately explicit; this extraction preserves the joint family group rather than assigning a child four biological parents or forcing respectively order.

Marīci/Sambhūti have Pūrṇamāsa and four daughters Kṛṣi,Vṛṣṭi,Kṛṣṭi,Apaciti; Pūrṇamāsa sons Virajas/Parvata. Pulaha/Kṣamā have Karmaśreṣṭha,Varīyas,Sahiṣṇu and Vanakavīnāsa (digital name retained as printed). Atri/Anasūyā have Soma,Durvāsas and yoga-bearing Datta, three deities described as Brahmā/Bhava/Viṣṇu kalāṃśas; individual matching is not forced from this collective stanza alone.

Aṅgiras/Smṛti have daughters Sinīvālī,Kuhū,Rākā,Anumati. Pulastya/Prīti have son Ayoni;45 mentions Devabāhu and a daughter with exact name/gender referent unresolved;44 mentions Agastya and a former birth with exact identity-direction unresolved. Kratu/Santati have60000 ūrdhvaretas Vālakhilya sons. Vasiṣṭha/Ūrjā have seven named sons Citraketu,Surocaka,Virajas,Mitra,Ulbana,Vasubhṛt,Ghumān (घुमान् digital), and an unnamed lotus-eyed daughter;48 also mentions other seven beginning Śakti. Names/count overlap and Ayoni–Agastya identity are retained for review, without forced merger.

Vahni is described Rudra-natured and fathers Pāvaka,Pavamāna,Śuci in Svāhā. Each produces15 sons, giving49 fires in total including three and root Agni; all partake in yajñas. Pavamāna is friction-produced, Pāvaka lightning, Śuci the fire heating in Sun; each includes sons. Agni is everywhere/Rudra-natured and Brahmā’s son. This enumeration is not split into49 invented individual names.

Pitṛs include formless Agniṣvāttas and embodied Barhiṣads. Svadhā bears them daughters Menā/Dharaṇī, both knowers of Brahman. Menā bears Maināka/Krauñca and Gaṅgā/Pārvatī to Himavat; both goddesses gain Śaṅkara as husband. Himavat/Menā worship Satī by tapas and receive Pārvatī as daughter by boon. Dharaṇī is Meru’s wife and bears Ayati/Niyati already named. Mudgala closes this Dakṣa-daughter lineage account, whose reading/hearing grants all wishes.

Fathers individually teach Gaṇeśa worship and varied prescribed mantras to Dakṣa-daughter descendants. They go to forest, perform tapas/Heramba-japa and gain Gaṇeśa appearance after1000 years (no divine qualifier). They hymn Brahman/yoga/peace, protector/creator/preserver/destroyer, beyond māyā while its mover, infinite face/arms and witness, requesting firm devotion ending delusion, capacity in their respective tasks and all wishes fulfilled. Gaṇeśa grants successful intentions, happy devotion, task-capacity and firm fame. He promises hymn users siddhi by faithful hearing/reading and immediate desired fruit from21 readings for21 days; disappears. All men/women descendants return home happy, knowledgeable and successful in tasks.

Śaunaka requests detailed accounts of Atri’s deity-natured sons. Sūta says Candra arises as Brahmā portion, performs tapas and receives Gaṇeśa’s boon making him nectar-formed. His kalās nourish gods/people and rays increase food growth. Requested wording/duration are unstated.

Datta, Viṣṇu kalāṃśa, attains successive Brahman/yoga states such as inert/mad/piśāca/child-joy states. People of all varṇas/āśramas serve him, leaving no rest; distressed he submerges by yoga while they wait at shore. By siddhi he manifests Mokṣalakṣmī, rises holding her at left and wine-pot in right, drinks/enjoys with her. They judge him fallen and abandon him, allowing peaceful yoga. This is a narrated withdrawal stratagem; Mokṣalakṣmī is not silently identified with Viṣṇu’s ordinary spouse.

A nearby god/demon battle defeats gods, who flee and beg Datta’s protection.35 names a surā group arriving with bare/drawn weapons and gods fleeing; that arrival’s agency is separately flagged. Demons seize beautiful Mokṣalakṣmī, deludedly carry her on their heads; source says placing her at feet would instead have given victory. They lose radiance, are pressed by gods, flee to Pātāla; goddess vanishes into Brahman. No actual feet-placement victory is narrated.

Śaunaka asks why head contact with Mokṣalakṣmī harms demons. Sūta gives Vyāsa-derived explanation: these rajas/tamas demons seek enjoyment, steal/commit sexual misconduct, harm beings, drink and revile sages/gods/scriptures; they reject liberation and honor Bhogalakṣmī with heads. Sages/gods seek liberation, honor her at head. Demons’ yogin contact brings Mokṣalakṣmī, but without desire for liberation and while vicious/pleasure-attached she is angry and destroys them; taking unwanted liberation is treated as striking her with feet. Enjoyment-seekers should honor enjoyment goddess; liberation-seekers similarly reject enjoyment. Bhogalakṣmī is vāsanā-full, Mokṣalakṣmī without vāsanā. These are attributed yogic interpretations, not a universal physical head-contact rule.
